<SUMMARY>
The global landscape this week is defined by an intensifying AI race, strategic competition for critical minerals, and the ongoing economic repercussions of the Middle East conflict. Major advancements in AI technology were seen from US companies like Microsoft (quantum computing, agentic AI) and Micron (high-capacity SSDs), while China's Huawei announced a chip design breakthrough and enacted strict controls on AI experts. Taiwan solidified its central role in the AI compute supply chain with significant investments from AMD and NVIDIA, alongside talks for deeper Taiwan-Korea AI ties. Simultaneously, the US Commerce Department admitted failures in enforcing AI export controls on China. Critical mineral supply chains are a focal point, with Japan pursuing deep-sea rare earths, the US securing a Greenland rare earth deal and establishing domestic processing facilities, and China maintaining pressure through rare earth curbs and new mining controls. The Middle East conflict continues to affect global energy markets, freight costs, and has led the OECD to slash global growth forecasts, projecting potential recessions and job losses in Europe. Regional geopolitical tensions persist, with China asserting maritime claims in the South China Sea and Russia posing a potential threat in the Arctic.
</SUMMARY>

<EWS>
The US Commerce Department admitted failure to enforce AI export controls on China, indicating a critical vulnerability in preventing technology transfer. The European Union’s €20 billion plan for five AI gigafactories is experiencing significant delays and funding issues, potentially hindering Europe's AI infrastructure development. Mounting anti-AI sentiment in the Americas is being monitored by law enforcement, with warnings of potential offline destructive actions. The ongoing Middle East conflict is projected by the OECD to slam the global economy into recession and could lead to 1.3 million job losses in the EU due to energy price surges. Indian MSMEs face significant setbacks, including anticipated decreases in production and revenue, directly linked to the West Asia conflict.
</EWS>

<EXEC>

**Asia:**
Huawei Technologies announced a chip design breakthrough on May 25, with an aim to produce industry-leading semiconductors within five years. Taiwan Semiconductor Manufacturing (TSMC) sits at the absolute center of the AI compute supply chain and is deepening AI chipmaker lock-in. NVIDIA's GTC Taiwan 2026 emphasized Taiwan's evolution from a supply chain participant to a co-designer in the AI factory era. AMD committed more than $10 billion to Taiwan’s AI supply chain. SK Group and Foxconn talks could signal deeper Taiwan-Korea AI supply chain ties. SK Hynix plans to double wafer capacity amid an AI memory shortage. Japan will develop a deep-sea drone to search for rare earth mineral resources in the seabed near remote islands. Prime Minister Sanae Takaichi announced on June 2nd that the government will significantly strengthen supplies of paint thinner and other chemical products by allowing raw materials to be supplied directly from petroleum refiners. China’s assimilation campaign in Inner Mongolia is now targeting the digital communities of Mongolian speakers. China is keeping rare earth pressure on Washington following the Trump Summit and is set to prolong rare-earth curbs and economic retaliation against Tokyo. China began imposing mining controls on strategic minerals starting June 15. The Commerce Department admitted failure to enforce AI export controls on China. China has added domestic AI chips to its "safe and reliable" procurement list to accelerate independence from US companies like Nvidia. SurplusGLOBAL secured Korean patents for AI-powered export control automation technology, strengthening safety in semiconductor equipment and parts transactions. China forbade top AI experts to leave the country without approval. China claimed it drove away a Dutch warship near the disputed Paracel Islands on May 30.

**Africa:**
The EU is betting billions on South Africa for critical minerals, while China tightens its grip on these resources. Africa is facing new competition for critical minerals investment as the US secured a rare earth deal in Greenland. GoldHaven Resources Corp. is targeting the historic Kuhn Tungsten Zone in a fully funded 2026 drill program. Two individuals were killed during protests in Kenya against a US Ebola facility.

**Europe:**
The European Union’s €20 billion plan for five AI gigafactories, each with one gigawatt of capacity and approximately 100,000 advanced chips, is encountering delays and funding issues, pushing the bidding process to July. STMicroelectronics shares surged over 15% as the company strengthens its AI infrastructure position and sees recovering demand in automotive and industrial markets. Foxconn, Radiall, and Thales inaugurated Tessalia to produce more than 50 million "made in Europe" components annually. Europe unveiled a sweeping tech sovereignty plan to boost chips and AI. The Norwegian defense minister warned that Russia could pose a grave risk if it gained control of the Arctic’s Bear Gap. China is attempting to turn Serbia into a European high-tech hub.

**Americas:**
Micron began shipping its 245TB 6600 ION NVMe SSD on May 5, positioning it as the highest-capacity commercially available drive. Microsoft unveiled Majorana 2, a next-generation topological quantum chip with qubits 1,000 times more reliable than its predecessor, cutting its timeline for a scalable quantum computer in half through the use of agentic AI. NVIDIA partnered with Microsoft on a unified stack for agentic AI deployment, ranging from Windows devices to cloud and local environments. Microsoft released MAI-Thinking-1 as one of seven new AI models, aiming to lessen reliance on OpenAI and lower costs for developers. Marvell Technology stock surged over 29% after Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang touted it as a potential trillion-dollar company during Computex Week. Samsung is relocating its US headquarters to Plano, Texas. Taiwan Semiconductor Manufacturing (TSMC) is weighing AI pricing power against overseas fab margin pressures. TSMC is also tapping Nvidia accelerated computing to drive next-gen semiconductor fabs. Intel's EMIB-T is stepping in to support Google's TPU supply chain due to strain on TSMC's CoWoS capacity. Polar Semiconductor and Nexperia partnered on US-based power MOSFET manufacturing for electric vehicles. Mink Ventures Corporation closed $881,920 in the first tranche of a non-brokered private placement. G50 Limited announced partial results from its drilling programs at the Golconda Project in Arizona, confirming significant high-grade gold and silver mineralization and consistent gallium. The US secured a Greenland rare earth deal in an effort to cut reliance on China. USA Rare Earth selected Cherokee County, South Carolina for a new rare earth metal and magnet manufacturing operation. USA Rare Earth is expanding its commitment to France with plans for additional investment in the French rare earth ecosystem, necessitating regional justification for placement here. USA Rare Earth Chief Global Policy Officer Gregory Bowman was appointed to the Department of War Science, Technology and Innovation Board. Secretary of State Marco Rubio stated that the United States is currently a global leader on AI but noted that this lead is not irreversible. A bulletin from a regional fusion center indicated that Philly Cops are monitoring increasing anti-AI sentiment on social media, warning that offline destructive action is anticipated.

**Oceania:**
CSIS released analyses on the Maven Smart System and the US struggle with its adversaries over the future of AI. The Atlantic Council Commission on AI laid out a roadmap for US leadership in AI.
</EXEC>

<CONCLUSION>
The global strategic environment remains highly dynamic, characterized by intense technological competition, particularly in advanced semiconductors and AI. Geopolitical tensions, notably the US-China rivalry and the ongoing Middle East conflict, are directly impacting global supply chains for critical minerals and energy, exacerbating economic uncertainties. Efforts to achieve technological sovereignty and supply chain resilience are driving significant state actions and investments across multiple regions, yet vulnerabilities, such as the US Commerce Department's admitted failure in export controls, persist. The economic fallout from geopolitical events, as evidenced by OECD warnings of recession and specific market impacts in Japan and Europe, underscores the interconnectedness of global security and economic stability.
</CONCLUSION>

<INDIA>
IT stocks led a recovery in Indian markets, reversing losses despite geopolitical tensions and foreign selling pressures. Crisil analysts anticipate that Indian MSMEs will bear a bigger hit than large firms from the West Asia conflict, facing significant setbacks, including anticipated decreases in production and revenue, due to mounting trade obstacles. India’s LNG imports are surging despite it being one of the most expensive Asian gas markets, defying a regional pattern of demand destruction. India's data center sector is experiencing rapid growth, leading to substantial land acquisitions across new markets, with major investments creating new infrastructure corridors driven by hyperscale cloud operators and AI providers. PepsiCo launched its premium energy drink, Adrenaline Rush, in the Indian market, expanding its beverage portfolio and targeting Gen-Z. The Enforcement Directorate (ED) conducted FEMA searches at four locations linked to Vedanta Ltd., including offices in Delhi, Mumbai, and Udaipur, Rajasthan. India’s semiconductor ecosystem is maturing, with ASML taking notice. Commentary suggests India's foreign policy choices are being reshaped by tech rivalry between the US and China and wars in the Middle East. An article highlights "Atmanirbhar vs Nirbhar Bharat."
</INDIA>

<WEST_ASIA>
The ongoing conflict in the Middle East is impacting global financial markets, with US stocks gaining as traders evaluated developments, and the Dow Jones Industrial Average climbing near record highs as AI optimism offset geopolitical risks. Oil prices swung higher as traders parsed discordant signals on the prospects of a US-Iran deal, with concerns over the Strait of Hormuz disruption and falling oil stockpiles driving the market. Copper topped $14,000 a ton and aluminum advanced to its highest in over four years due to optimism over demand and supply constraints, outweighing concerns over the unresolved conflict. The OECD slashed its global growth forecast, warning that the Iran war could slam the global economy into recession, and the EU could lose 1.3 million jobs due to energy price surges linked to the conflict. The head of the Operations Division in the Military Intelligence Directorate stated that the Intelligence Directorate failed to provide warning ahead of the October 7 attack. Israel is adding to its constant ceasefire violations with plans to take more of Gaza. Qatar shut down natural gas production, contributing to India’s surging LNG imports despite costly gas. UAE lenders are leading the way in Middle East AI adoption. The UAE expanded its AI push with a new leadership development program. In Saudi Arabia’s Year of AI, business leaders are seeking trusted partners. Iran faces a new energy imbalance, but its options are limited. The Tribeca Festival 2026 accepted "Dreams of Violets," a fully AI-generated feature, into its official lineup. Treasuries pared gains after jobs openings backed a rate-hike view, influenced by Middle East developments.
</WEST_ASIA>

<FINAL_CONCLUSION>
The confluence of accelerating AI development, intense competition for critical resources, and persistent geopolitical friction is setting the strategic agenda. The race for technological leadership, particularly in semiconductors and AI, will continue to drive state-level investments and policy interventions, increasingly entwined with national security imperatives. Supply chain vulnerabilities, especially for rare earths and advanced chips, will remain a critical focus, prompting further diversification and domestic production efforts. The economic impacts of regional conflicts, exemplified by the Middle East, will continue to ripple globally, demanding agile responses to safeguard economic stability and energy security. The need for robust export control mechanisms and comprehensive strategies to manage emerging technological risks will intensify.
</FINAL_CONCLUSION>
